Did you receive a Medicare Annual Notice of Change (ANOC) in the mail? Don't throw it away! Your Medicare Advantage or Part D prescription drug plan may be changing for 2027 — even if your plan name stays the same.

In today's Marcus Retires video, we explain 5 important changes hiding inside your Medicare letter that could affect your monthly premiums, medical bills, prescription drug costs, doctor network, and coverage for next year.

Medicare Open Enrollment runs from October 15 through December 7, 2026. During this period, eligible beneficiaries can review and change their Medicare Advantage and prescription drug coverage for 2027.

THE 5 MEDICARE CHANGES YOU NEED TO CHECK:

1️⃣ MONTHLY PREMIUM CHANGES

Your Medicare Advantage or Part D premium may increase or decrease in 2027. A lower premium doesn't always mean lower total healthcare costs.

2️⃣ MAXIMUM OUT-OF-POCKET COSTS

Check your Medicare Advantage plan's annual out-of-pocket maximum. A higher limit could mean greater financial exposure during a year with expensive medical treatment.

3️⃣ PRESCRIPTION DRUG DEDUCTIBLES AND COSTS

Review your 2027 drug deductible, prescription tiers, covered medications, and annual Part D out-of-pocket limit. Learn how the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan may help spread eligible costs across the year.

4️⃣ MEDICARE ADVANTAGE PLAN TERMINATIONS

Some Medicare Advantage plans are discontinuing coverage or leaving certain service areas for 2027. If your plan is ending, you may have additional enrollment options and deadlines.

5️⃣ DOCTOR NETWORKS AND DRUG FORMULARIES

Your doctors, hospitals, pharmacies, and prescriptions may not have the same coverage next year. Always verify your exact plan and medications before making a decision.

description:
📘 Get the Guide 👇marcusretires.com

October is the busiest month of the year for anyone on Social Security and Medicare, and this year it holds six real deadlines. It also arrives with noise — claims that your benefit is being cut in October, that you must verify your account or lose it, that a new rule is coming for your savings. Almost none of that is true. So this is a calendar: date by date, what is changing, who it reaches, and the one thing to do.

🔹 31 October — a savings deadline. I bond rates reset on 1 November, so buying by the end of October locks in the current rate for six months. If a CD matures, do not let it roll over automatically — banks often renew below their best rate. And interest counts as income: it affects how much of your Social Security is taxed and can raise your Medicare premium two years later.

🔹 Start now, finish by 31 December. Required minimum distributions for anyone 73 or older — miss one and the penalty is 25 percent, reduced to 10 if corrected. And for anyone 70½ or older who gives to charity, a distribution sent straight from the IRA to the charity counts toward the required withdrawal without adding to taxable income.

🔹 Ten minutes this month. Set up your own my Social Security account before somebody opens one in your name, and arrange direct deposit if you still get a paper check. Your notice for next year appears there before the letter arrives.

🔹 The October scam aimed at savings. A call, text or pop-up says your bank account has a problem. You are passed to a fraud department and told to move your savings to a safe account, withdraw cash, or buy gold for a courier — and to tell no one, not even your bank. All of it is a lie. No bank and no agency will ever ask you to move money to protect it or keep it secret. Deposits are insured to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category.

💡 Three things that are not happening: your benefit is not being cut in October · the automatic 4 percent Medicare cut was cleared away last November · and Social Security is not running out this year — the retirement fund is projected to run short in late 2032, at about 78 percent payable without action.
